messages:
ashley: hitting a weird client report — streaming SSE sessions abruptly cut with a mid-stream 429. customer says tokens kept counting up on their side, but our billing shows less. they repro reliably after ~30–45s of stream. attaching logs below. anyone seen this pattern?

ben: can you drop the raw request/response? specifically the SSE frames and headers. 429 mid-stream usually means quota enforcement hit on our edge or an auth token refresh hiccup.

ashley: pasted. note we proxied via our api-gateway (eu-west) to hosted inference. request id: rq_8f2b. client uses long-lived API key, reconnects with same key.

ashley: ```
REQ HEADERS:
:method: GET
:path: /v1/streams/generate
authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
accept: text/event-stream
user-agent: AcmeClient/1.3

SSE FRAMES (partial):
event: message
data: {"delta":"Hello"}
event: message
data: {"delta":" world"}

then 3xx keepalives, then:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\r\ncontent-type: application/json\r\nretry-after: 10\r\n{"error":{"message":"quota exceeded","code":429}}
```

maria: interesting — the SSE stream closes with 429 but the client reports it continued to receive tokens and increments its local counters. could be a reconnect that resumed a different cursor/segment and the client dedup logic double-counted? or the client kept reading a TCP buffer after the connection was closed?

chandra: on our infra side, I see a burst of rate-limited responses for that org (org_793) from the gateway at 1708200037. Gateway returned 429 then closed connection. Downstream serving logs show the model produced until ~1708200040 but we didn't emit SSE after the gateway sent 429. Potential race between quota check and streaming buffer flush.

infra-bot: note: policy-enforcer v2.1 rolled at 1708199400 to edge nodes — added per-token quota short-circuit. See job: policy-enforcer/roll/1708199400.

ben: that aligns. new short-circuit path checks quota before every chunk; if quota decision flips mid-stream (e.g., usage race with an embedding request), gateway immediately responds 429 and tears down the connection. If the server had already buffered a few SSE frames, they might be delivered to client TCP stack even after the HTTP socket shutdown, so client libs may count them. So billing (which counts tokens when accepted by the control plane) could differ from what the client reads.

lisa-billing: can you paste the customer's reported token counts vs our billing numbers? we need examples to reconcile.

ashley: customer says client saw 812 tokens for session X, but our billing shows 637 tokens ingested for the same session. They expect a refund or explanation.

maria: two hypotheses:
1) client buffered TCP payload after we closed connection (client counted bytes read, not server-accepted tokens).
2) client retried/resumed and counted duplicates.
We need repro steps. ashley can you try toggling a simulated quota hit mid-stream from gateway and capture pcaps or tcpdump at gateway?

ashley: doing a live repro now with curl/ncat and with our JS SDK to see behavior. steps: start stream, send a large prompt, then in parallel simulate a quota delta event to trigger quota_exceeded on gateway. Will collect curl --raw output and tcpdump.

ashley: quick findings: with curl --raw I see SSE frames until the 429 arrives, then curl prints the JSON body and exits. The bytes after the 429 are not part of a new SSE frame. With node SDK (EventSource polyfill) the onmessage handler got two extra delta chunks that were in flight right before the connection close.

chandra: that matches TCP semantics — packets in flight can be delivered even across a close if server did a write then close; or if keepalive sent. If billing increments tokens when the control plane reconciles accepted tokens (post-chunk ack), the numbers will mismatch if client counts raw stream bytes.

ben: mitigation options:
- change quota enforcement to allow graceful finish of in-flight chunk before returning 429 (buffer-aware enforcement).
- ensure we immediately send an SSE "event: error" frame before HTTP 429 so clients have deterministic case to stop counting. (but proxies may not forward if we change status code).
- update SDKs & docs to recommend counting tokens from server meta events or on final confirmation rather than raw stream bytes (client-side change).

maria: for now, quick customer workaround: tell them to rely on our post-session usage record (we expose per-session token usage via /v1/usage/session/:id) rather than client-side counting. Also advise SDK update to ignore incomplete final chunks on abnormal closes.

lisa-billing: we should offer a one-time credit if the delta > 20% and they can provide request ids. I'll draft an email once we confirm logs.

ashley: reproducer notes (for infra runbook):
1) start long SSE stream with token-heavy prompt (5000+ expected tokens).
2) trigger org quota decrement from admin console or simulate a concurrent heavy request that exhausts commit.
3) observe gateway logs: policy-enforcer returns 429 with request id. Capture tcpdump on 10.0.3.x edge node.
4) compare client-side token count vs /v1/usage/session/:id and gateway accepted-token logs.

chandra: added: ensure to capture sequence numbers so we can map SSE frame boundaries to token counts. Use our debug header X-Debug-Trace: true to get chunk-token tags in logs.

ben: followup todos:
- chandra/infra: add a short-term toggle to policy-enforcer to delay 429 until current chunk flush (low-risk config) — target ETA 48h.
- devex/maria: add SDK guidance and a small patch to ignore partial chunk after abnormal close — ETA 1 week.
- billing/lisa: ready a provisional credit flow and finalize after log verification.
- support/ashley: send customer initial explanation and ask for request ids and pcaps.

ashley: pinging customer now. will attach logs. thanks. :heavy_check_mark:

maria: one more note — for audit: we should record when a 429 is served mid-stream and tag session with termination_reason=quota_midstream so downstream accounting knows to reconcile differently. filing internal ticket INF-1227.

ashley: thanks all. closing when I get confirmation from customer or we push the infra toggle.

lisa-billing: marked followup with billing ops.

infra-bot: INF-1227 created by maria at 1708200500. link: https://redwood.internal/infra/INF-1227
